payload.reason: The evidence explains that higher absolute accuracy numbers compared to F1 scores indicate that human evaluations can assess correctness more comprehensively than automatic evaluations, which may miss some correct answers.

claims.text: Higher absolute accuracy numbers than F1 scores suggest that human evaluations capture more correct answers than automatic evaluations, which often miss valid responses due to limited gold answer sets.

The discrepancy arises because human annotators can evaluate correctness more effectively than automatic systems, which rely on predefined gold answers that may not encompass all possible correct responses.
